title: The Burnt Cipher
premise: Theo Oyelaran, a deniable fixer for a shadowy London-based 'trade liaison office,' receives calls on a burner phone from Mara Voss, her former handler and the woman who trained her — a woman officially dead for six years. Mara claims the network, codenamed LANTERN, has been sold to a private consortium and that Theo's own recruitment file is being auctioned as leverage. As Theo races through Vienna, Zurich, and Frankfurt to verify the claim, she discovers Mara is both warning her and using her: the calls are bait in Mara's private war against the man who erased her. In the end, Theo must choose between loyalty to the mentor who made her and the truth that the network was always disposable people like them; she burns LANTERN's ledger before the Frankfurt markets open, exposes the sale, and walks away with nothing official — but finally belonging to herself.
about_author: Dominic Winterbourne is the pen name of a former risk consultant who spent a decade advising firms on geopolitical exposure across Europe. He writes thrillers about the paperwork behind the violence, and lives in Edinburgh with an unclassified number of houseplants.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Theo Oyelaran's POV. A routine Tuesday at the 'Trade Liaison Office': shredding a diplomat's mistake, packing the go-bag she never unpacks. Establishes her polished lie of a life and her rule never to look back. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Number Not in the Book
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. An unknown burner rings her personal line — a line almost no one has. The voice is Mara Voss, dead six years, saying only: 'You have until the markets open.' Theo checks the obituary again. Beat: vertigo beneath composure.

chapters.title: What the Office Denies
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, with a brief interlude from her deputy Callum. She probes colleagues for any record of Voss; files are clean, too clean. Callum notices her distraction. Beat: first crack in trust.

chapters.title: Second Call: Vienna
chapters.summary: Mara directs Theo to a left-luggage locker in Vienna containing a partial copy of her own recruitment file — redacted by someone who knew exactly what to hide. Beat: the past has fingerprints.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Made Me
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Theo's POV. Training under Mara: tradecraft, loyalty drills, the lesson 'the network is the only family you get.' Beat: tenderness braided with indoctrination.

chapters.title: Locker 44
chapters.summary: Theo in Vienna, retrieving the file while watching for tails. She spots a surveillance pattern too professional to be police, too sloppy to be LANTERN. Beat: hunted without proof.

chapters.title: Auction House
chapters.summary: New POV: Ilse Brandt, a Zurich data broker, cataloguing lots for a private sale — including personnel dossiers from a defunct state program. One lot is flagged 'O.' Beat: cold commerce of human lives.

chapters.title: Deniable Everything
chapters.summary: Theo confronts her director, Hargreaves, who denies LANTERN exists while sweating through his shirt. He offers her a promotion to stop asking. Beat: the institution gaslights its own.

chapters.title: Third Call: Proof of Life
chapters.summary: Mara gives Theo a detail only the real Mara could know — the words Theo said the night she was recruited. Theo stops doubting the voice and starts doubting everything else. Beat: grief re-ignited.

chapters.title: Zurich, Quietly
chapters.summary: Theo flies to Zurich off-book, using old training to travel ghost-clean. First time in years she feels alive. Beat: the addict's comfort of tradecraft.

chapters.title: The Broker's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Theo approaches her posing as a buyer's agent. Ilse, sharp and amoral, smells the desperation but plays along. Beat: two liars sizing each other up.

chapters.title: Lot Nineteen
chapters.summary: Theo views Lot 19: her file, plus eleven others — the full roster of LANTERN assets, all marked 'expendable post-sale.' Beat: rage crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Who Sold the Family
chapters.summary: Mara's fourth call: she names the seller — Deputy Director Ashcombe, the man who ran LANTERN after Mara's 'death' and now sits on the oversight board. Beat: betrayal given a face.

chapters.title: Ashcombe
chapters.summary: Ashcombe's POV. He learns someone accessed the archive and quietly activates cleanup assets — including, unknowingly, people assigned to watch Theo. Beat: patient menace.

chapters.title: Tail in the Old Town
chapters.summary: Theo runs a counter-surveillance loop through Zurich's alleys, loses one tail, clocks another. Callum calls from London: 'People are asking about your travel.' Beat: no safe ground.

chapters.title: The Price of the File
chapters.summary: Ilse names her price for Lot 19: not money — introduction to a buyer Theo can reach. Theo realizes everyone wants something. Beat: transactional world, transactional heart.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Theo and Mara arrange a meet via dead-drop protocol they invented years ago. Anticipation, dread, and the fear that meeting will break the spell. Beat: love and suspicion entwined.

chapters.title: The Train to Basel
chapters.summary: The meet: Mara, older, scarred, alive. She explains LANTERN was sold because it was always a liability — and that Theo's file is the key to unwinding the sale. Beat: reunion shot through with doubt.

chapters.title: Why She Died
chapters.summary: Mara's account: she discovered the sale, faked her death when Ashcombe moved to erase her, and has spent six years positioning. Theo hears both testimony and manipulation. Beat: the mentor as unreliable narrator.

chapters.title: Cleanup Crew
chapters.summary: LANTERN's remaining assets are activated against Theo. A near-miss assassination in Basel forces her and Mara to run together. Beat: the family turned weapon.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Holed up, Theo and Mara plan. Mara needs Theo's access codes; Theo needs Mara's evidence. Neither says it aloud. Beat: intimacy as negotiation.

chapters.title: Callum's Choice
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Pressed by Hargreaves to report Theo's movements, he stalls, then warns her with a coded phrase from their shared history. Beat: small loyalties mattering enormously.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Before Dawn
chapters.summary: The team relocates to Frankfurt; the sale closes when markets open in thirty-six hours. Mara reveals the ledger's location inside the consortium's data vault. Beat: clock starts audibly ticking.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Bank
chapters.summary: Recon of the consortium's private vault: biometrics, air-gapped systems, a twenty-minute window during a shareholder gala. Beat: heist-shaped hope.

chapters.title: Gala Dress, Loaded Past
chapters.summary: Theo infiltrates the gala as a consultant's plus-one, trading on the polished lie she's perfected. She sees Ashcombe arrive. Beat: mask over mask.

chapters.title: Twenty Minutes
chapters.summary: The vault breach begins. Mara works the systems; Theo covers the door. They get ninety percent of the ledger before alarms trip early. Beat: triumph curdling.

chapters.title: Betrayal, Itemized
chapters.summary: The early alarm wasn't accident: Mara triggered it to force Theo's hand, burning her cover so Theo could never go back to the Office. Beat: fury — the mentor sacrificed her again, for her own good.

chapters.title: Split
chapters.summary: Theo and Mara separate under fire. Theo, half the ledger, and a burned identity. Mara takes the other half toward a second buyer. Beat: abandonment as inheritance.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: Ashcombe's people catch Callum instead. His POV under pressure: he gives up nothing that matters and something that does. Beat: ordinary courage.

chapters.title: Reading the Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo deciphers her half: payments, erasures, and proof that every asset — herself included — was written into the sale as inventory. Beat: the theme lands: loyalty was the product.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Ashcombe reaches out directly: return the ledger, get reinstated, get a real life. It's tempting precisely because it's sincere. Beat: the devil offering a home.

chapters.title: What Mara Never Said
chapters.summary: Theo finds a discrepancy proving Mara helped design the expendability clause years ago — then fought it too late. Truth without absolution. Beat: disillusionment as maturity.

chapters.title: Counter-Bid
chapters.summary: Theo flips the auction: she offers Ilse the complete story instead of the file, turning the broker into a witness. Beat: weaponizing transparency.

chapters.title: Markets Open in Six Hours
chapters.summary: Final assembly: Theo must reunite the ledger halves with Mara before the Frankfurt open, knowing Mara may sell her out. Beat: decision point.

chapters.title: Rooftop Reckoning
chapters.summary: Theo and Mara meet above the exchange. Guns, history, honesty at last. Mara admits she used Theo and loved her, in whichever order is worse. Beat: the climax's emotional core.

chapters.title: Burn Protocol
chapters.summary: Together they inject the full ledger into public financial feeds minutes before opening bell — the sale collapses, consortium investors flee, Ashcombe's protection evaporates. Beat: catharsis through exposure.

chapters.title: Ashcombe Falls Quietly
chapters.summary: No arrest, no trial: Ashcombe is simply retired by the institution that used him, erased as cleanly as he erased others. Theo watches from a distance. Beat: justice as irony.

chapters.title: What Callum Knows
chapters.summary: Back in London, Callum covers Theo's traces and asks no questions. A quiet scene between colleagues who will never speak of it. Beat: grace in the margins.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Theo unpacks the go-bag for the first time in years — not because she's safe, but because she's done living packed. Mara sends one last burner; Theo lets it ring. Beat: release.

chapters.title: The Cipher That Remains
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Theo's POV. Months later, a new recruit arrives at the Office; Theo trains her with Mara's lessons revised by hard-won truth: belong to yourself first. Final beat: memory kept, loyalty earned, truth carried forward.
